_why: Measured state of the mission's offline promise, kept in the repo so a passing build is not mistaken for a kept promise.
method: Chrome DevTools Protocol (playwright is not installed on the build host): load the built game from a local static server, warm the cache, set Network.emulateNetworkConditions offline=true, reload, and read window.__GAME__ and the active scene list.

result.observed: Chrome's ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED page. window.__GAME__ absent, zero active scenes.

why_it_fails: Nothing caches the game. Every request is same-origin under the game's own directory, which is necessary for offline play but not sufficient: without a service worker the browser still has to reach the server, so a cold reload with no network cannot even fetch index.html.
what_is_gated_today: check:selfhosted asserts the precondition that is true and worth keeping: every asset path a bundle names exists in dist and none is cross-origin. It deliberately does NOT claim the games boot offline.
to_make_it_true: Add a service worker per game that precaches the cold-load set (index.html, the JS chunks, the fonts) on install and serves it cache-first, then caches audio and sprites on first use.
Register it from the game's entry point, and keep the registration a no-op when the page is not served over http(s) so a file:// open still works.
Extend this gate to drive the CDP offline probe once a worker exists, so the claim is measured rather than asserted.
